revenue: unknown (not broken out by parent; Clay estimate USD 200M-1B)
marketing_evidence: little evidence of sponsorship; product-led marketing
rationale: Evernote is a product brand of Bending Spoons (acquired 2023); the parent's prospectus gives growth rates only (+34% 2024, +30% 2025), not absolute Evernote revenue. A global productivity audience, but no stand-alone financials, and sponsorship decisions would sit with the parent.
parent: Bending Spoons (Nasdaq IPO Jul 2026 at about USD 18B valuation; 2025 revenue reported at USD 1.3B-2.6B, sources conflict)

rationale: Listed (not private) Hyderabad maker of microwave/RF subsystems for Indian defence and space, with about USD 132M revenue, healthy profit and a USD 1.8B market cap. Its customers are government defence agencies, so it has almost no consumer or F1 audience overlap.

revenue: USD 2.7B (INR 28,000 crore) (Wikipedia infobox, year not stated)
valuation: unknown for group (total equity USD 6.9B per Wikipedia; controls listed Britannia Industries, Bombay Dyeing)
profitability: Mixed: Britannia highly profitable; Go First airline in insolvency since 2023 (knowledge)
marketing_evidence: Owns IPL franchise Punjab Kings; Britannia is a major Indian advertiser
rationale: Privately held Wadia family conglomerate (Britannia, Bombay Dyeing, Punjab Kings) with about USD 2.7B revenue per Wikipedia. Large sports-marketing experience, but the group is India-centric and its brands are mass-market rather than premium.

revenue: NOK 25.7B (~USD 2.4B) operating revenue (2025, Strawberry group per Wikipedia; scope unclear)
marketing_evidence: Naming rights to Stockholm national stadium (Strawberry Arena) since Jan 2024
rationale: Nordic Choice Hotels was renamed Strawberry in May 2023 and runs about 257 hotels in the Nordics and Baltics, with roughly NOK 25.7B group revenue per Wikipedia. Its big stadium naming deal shows sponsorship appetite, but its footprint is regional only.

profitability: Net income BRL 136M (FY2025) after earlier losses
marketing_evidence: consumer brand marketing in Brazil (Multi); no major sports deal confirmed
rationale: B3-listed (not private) Brazilian consumer-electronics and gadgets group (brand Multi) with about USD 740M revenue and a return to profit in 2025. A Brazil-only footprint limits F1 fit beyond São Paulo GP activation.

marketing_evidence: major Indian broadcaster and advertiser; no current F1-scale sponsorship found
rationale: Zee Telefilms is the former name of Zee Entertainment Enterprises, an Indian broadcaster with about USD 920M revenue but sharply lower FY2026 profit and a sub-USD 1B market cap. Its audience is mass-market South Asian, so F1 overlap is limited.

marketing_evidence: ARY Digital Network owns PSL cricket franchise Karachi Kings (knowledge)
rationale: Pakistani TV network of ARY Group, with diaspora channels in the UK, UAE and US; no published revenue. Cricket franchise ownership shows sports appetite, but its audience and finances are an uncertain fit for F1.

marketing_evidence: national cinema advertising/promotions; US arm CMX Cinemas; no major sports deal found
rationale: Mexico's second-largest cinema chain (about 335 complexes) with MXN 23.5B revenue in 2024 per the Expansión 500 ranking; privately controlled by the Larrea family. It could activate around the Mexico City GP, but its reach is mainly domestic.

valuation: GEMS Education reportedly valued up to USD 6B in earlier stake-sale talks (dated, not confirmed)
marketing_evidence: GEMS brand marketing; Varkey Foundation Global Teacher Prize
rationale: Sunny Varkey's holding company controlling GEMS Education (52 schools, 170,000 students in the UAE, Qatar and Egypt; Brookfield-led consortium invested 2024). It has an affluent Gulf expat audience near the Abu Dhabi/Qatar GPs, but its finances are undisclosed and it is refinancing debt.

company: GUANGDONG CHIGO REFRIGERATION EQUIPMENT CO., LTD.
revenue: unknown (Clay estimate USD 500M+; last public figure RMB 4.66B H1 2010)
profitability: unknown; former HK-listed parent Chigo Holding suffered financial distress and delisting (knowledge, not re-verified)
rationale: Foshan-based air-conditioner maker (Chigo brand, founded 1994) that exports to emerging markets; no current financials are published, and its former listed parent had a reported financial crisis. A weak prospect on both fit and capacity.
